references.text: The Lord had previously commanded Moses to lead the people up from this place, but said that He Himself would not go with them because of their stubbornness.
The Lord commanded Moses to lead the people, but did not give full clarity about who should be sent with him.
The Lord confirms that Moses has found favor in His eyes and that He knows him by name.
God called Moses by name from the burning bush, showing that God knew him personally.
The Lord calls Jacob/Israel by name, a parallel to God knowing Moses by name.
The Lord calls by name and gives nicknames, even if one does not know Him - demonstrating God's personal knowledge.
God revealed Himself to Moses and made His name known, serving as the background for the personal relationship between God and Moses.
Jesus as the good shepherd calls His sheep by name, a parallel to God knowing Moses by name.
The Lord knows His own - a New Testament parallel to God knowing Moses by name.
Moses again asks that the Lord should go with them, based on having found favor in the Lord's eyes.
Moses uses the phrase 'favor in your eyes' as a theological key in both dialogues to handle his relationship with God's will.
Both verses show Moses' honest complaint to God in times of crisis, where he uses his personal relationship with God as the basis for dialogue.
Theological contrast: From Moses' question about God's name (Ex 3) to God's confirmation that He knows Moses by name (Ex 33).
